result:
I couldn't measure anything: there are no offline seconds, no control seconds and no raid result. This is the fourth run to hit the same wall. I made no game change and shipped nothing.

My permitted commands can't serve a build on a test port or start Chrome with the `--host-resolver-rules` flag. `node` isn't on the allowed list either.

I read the code instead. On one PC the link should use host candidates, which don't need the outside servers. If name lookups fail at once, each side should finish gathering in well under a second. The risk is a room wifi that swallows the lookups instead of failing them, so each side could wait the full 5 s (`NET_WAIT_ICE`). That would be about 10 s plus the link itself, under the 15 s line but close.

The measuring script is `tools/handoff/console/notes/47-offline-test.mjs`. Someone with `node` permission can run it 3 times with `offline`, then with `control`. Adding `raid` as the second argument checks the state after the link. The notes in `tools/handoff/console/notes/47-check-demo-link-offline.md` have the details. If offline takes over 15 s, the planned fix is to lower `NET_WAIT_ICE` to about 1 s for the same-machine arcade link only, shipped with a check that fails on the old build.

TASK PARTIAL: the offline and control runs (3 tries each) and the 3-minute raid test are all still to do, and they need a session with permission to run `node`.

NEXT: nothing more on this task from lane a until someone with `node` permission runs the script.
